summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow tax-exempt bonds to be used for private or commercial golf courses and country clubs, removing current restrictions on such use.

scores.thoughts: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to remove restrictions on the use of certain proceeds for golf courses and country clubs, which could indirectly affect tax-exempt bond financing or other tax-related incentives. This change would likely lead to a slight reduction in the tax base or an increase in tax-advantaged activities, thus leaning towards lower taxes for specific entities.

The bill removes a restriction preventing tax-exempt bond proceeds from financing private golf courses and country clubs. This expands eligibility for tax-preferred financing, increasing federal tax expenditures and thereby widening the deficit to accommodate these facilities.
